head: working-tree
subject: gRPC owned unary request storage
change: UnaryCallOptions gains owned_message backed by grpc.OwnedRequestMessage, prefix-reserved storage that a client serializes into directly. An identity unary request hands that exact allocation to the HTTP/2 writer, removing the framed staging copy of the whole request; compressed requests still allocate a separate framed buffer, and the borrowed message field keeps the existing staging path. The buffer is borrowed for the synchronous write and remains caller-owned, so a persistent client reuses one allocation across requests. SharedChannel queues jobs that may outlive the caller, so Job.create copies the owned payload into job-owned queued storage and leaves the caller's buffer reusable.

unit: src/grpc/runtime_tests.zig runs a real h2c server that checks an owned 13-byte request payload and answers the call.
src/grpc/channel/shared/tests.zig runs a SharedChannel unary call whose server checks the owned request payload, covering the queued copy path.

benchmark.order: alternating staged/owned and owned/staged per mode
benchmark.workload: 256 KiB request and response, full-byte response validation, server request length and first-byte validation, 20 warmups, 200 measured calls

notes: The benchmark compares request storage with the same binary and server: only the client request ownership changes. The staged path compresses/copies the payload and frames it per request; the owned path reuses one prefix-reserved buffer and performs no per-request payload copy or allocation. A request with both message and owned_message is rejected as InvalidMessageCount, and compressed requests still take the framed fallback. SharedChannel's queued-job copy is intentional because a job can outlive the caller after abandonment; the shared arm therefore measures parity rather than the ordinary zero-copy win.
